name: Noadiah
source_summary: A false prophetess who, along with other hired prophets, tried to intimidate and frighten Nehemiah in order to stop the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall.
family_friendly_summary: While Nehemiah and the people of Jerusalem were working hard to rebuild the city's broken walls, some enemies tried everything they could to stop them -- including scaring them. A woman named Noadiah, who claimed to be a prophetess, joined with other prophets in trying to frighten Nehemiah so he would give up or make a mistake. Nehemiah didn't let their scare tactics stop him. Instead, he prayed and asked God to remember what they had tried to do. The wall was finished anyway. Noadiah's story is a reminder that not everyone who claims to speak for God is telling the truth.
adult_story: Noadiah appears in Nehemiah's prayer near the end of his memoir of rebuilding Jerusalem's wall, named as one of several opponents who tried to derail the project through intimidation rather than open attack. After enemies like Sanballat and Tobiah failed to stop the work by force or mockery, they turned to psychological pressure -- hired false prophets and threatening pressure meant to make Nehemiah "afraid" and cause him to sin by fleeing into the temple in violation of the law, which would have discredited him (Nehemiah 6:10-13). Nehemiah names Noadiah the prophetess alongside "the rest of the prophets who were trying to frighten me" as part of this campaign (6:14), asking God to remember their deeds against him. Unlike true prophetesses in Scripture such as Deborah or Huldah, Noadiah used a claimed prophetic voice to oppose God's work rather than to speak His truth -- a warning, consistent with the Old Testament's repeated concern about false prophecy (compare Ezekiel 13, Jeremiah 28), that a prophetic title alone guarantees nothing. Nehemiah refused to be moved by fear and completed the wall in fifty-two days (6:15), and his brief prayer naming Noadiah stands as Scripture's only word about her.

devotionals: Noadiah used a claimed prophetic voice to frighten God's people away from His work. Jesus warned us that not everyone speaking in God's name tells the truth.
Nehemiah refused to let Noadiah's fear tactics stop God's work, and the wall was finished anyway. May we trust that Jesus's purposes can't be frightened off course.
